Name: synthesizability_blindspot_steering
Title: The Synthesizability Tax: Does Interpretable-Feature Property-Steering Systematically Trade Manufacturability for Target Gains, and Is Synthesizability Itself a Steerable Direction?
Short Hypothesis: We advance three separable claims. (C1, phenomenon) When an interpretable SAE feature is steered to improve a target property (logP, QED, docking, a functional group) of a generated molecule, generation drifts systematically—not randomly—toward less synthesizable chemical space; this 'synthesizability tax' has a measurable dose-response and same-sign structure across features. (C2, blind spot) Standard output-side checks a practitioner actually runs (RDKit validity, property-predictor confidence, generation log-likelihood) carry near-zero information about this tax, so the manufacturability loss is invisible to normal evaluation. (C3, mechanism) Synthesizability is linearly decodable from activations yet, under the intervention families we test, we do NOT find a robust direction that steers it the way logP/QED can—i.e., it behaves as a decodable-but-weakly-steerable global property. We deliberately scope C3 as 'no robust steerable direction found under tested interventions,' not a universal absence claim.
Related Work: Synthesizability is 'the elephant in the lab': generative models routinely propose unmakeable molecules, addressed via post-hoc filtering (RAscore 2021, RetroGNN 2020), retrosynthesis-constrained generation (building-block assembly 2023, TANGO 2024, steerable synthesizability control 2025, SynTwins 2025), and retrosynthesis-in-the-loop optimization (2024). These are architecture/objective interventions treating synthesizability as an external constraint on the MODEL. A second line—molecular-LM interpretability (SynFlowNet interpretability 2025, 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' 2025, token-level KL importance 2025)—shows physicochemical properties are linearly decodable and steerable. A third, general-interpretability line studies decodability-vs-causality: a probe reading a concept does not imply an intervention can steer it (activation patching, difference-of-means steering, SAE feature ablation). Positioning as a three-row contrast: (i) synthesizability-control papers CHANGE the model to make it steerable—we FREEZE the model and ask what interpretable steering costs; (ii) molecular-LM steering papers steer desired properties but never audit the synthesizability side-effect nor test synthesizability's own steerability; (iii) decodability-vs-causality papers give our diagnostic frame but were not applied to a chemical global property with real manufacturing stakes. No prior work quantifies a property-vs-synthesizability tradeoff induced by interpretable-feature steering, tests synthesizability's causal steerability head-to-head against physicochemical properties at matched decodability, or ships a reusable audit for it. Our contribution is thus threefold and clearly typed: a new empirical phenomenon (C1), a mechanistic diagnosis (C3), and a released audit/benchmark protocol—not a new generation method.
Abstract: Generative molecular design has a notorious blind spot: models propose molecules that cannot be made, 'the elephant in the lab.' The field fights this with retrosynthesis filters and synthesis-constrained generation, but no one has asked what happens to synthesizability when practitioners use the increasingly popular interpretable-feature steering to hit a target property. We surface and explain a phenomenon we call the synthesizability tax: steering an interpretable SAE feature to improve a desired property (logP, QED, docking, a functional group) systematically drags generation into less synthesizable chemical space, and the property-focused evaluations practitioners run never see it. We make three separable, pre-registered claims: (C1) the tax is systematic with a dose-response, not generic drift; (C2) cheap output-side checks are near-blind to it; and (C3) synthesizability is linearly decodable from activations yet, under all intervention families we test, has no robust steerable direction—unlike logP/QED at matched decodability. Using frozen autoregressive SMILES chemical language models with sparse autoencoders and cheap synthesizability oracles (SAscore, RAscore) validated against a retrosynthesis planner (AiZynthFinder route-found rate and route length) on stratified subsets, we quantify the tax with per-property normalized effect sizes; separate it from off-distribution drift using non-interpretable latent-steering, KL-matched, and temperature controls; test synthesizability's steerability head-to-head against physicochemical properties; and evaluate an orthogonalization mitigation with a pre-set success bar. Deliverable: an open audit suite that flags unmakeable steered designs before expensive retrosynthesis. Either outcome is actionable—a real tax changes steering evaluation protocols; a null result certifies interpretable steering as synthesizability-safe.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: a GPT-style autoregressive SMILES chemical language model, either public (MolGPT, ~6M) or trained by us (~15M, 8 layers, d=512) on ZINC-250k (249,455 molecules; 80/10/10 split by scaffold to prevent leakage). Base model FROZEN; only inference-time steering vectors added. Directions from TopK sparse autoencoders (over-complete dictionary reconstructing the residual stream with top-k active latents): expansion 16x, k=32, trained on 30M mid-layer residual vectors (layer picked by max intrinsic dimension; one alternative layer kept), Adam lr 3e-4, batch 4096, seeds 0/1/2. Steering = add alpha*d_hat to the residual during decoding; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8,16} residual-RMS units. Oracles (RDKit): logP, QED, MW, ring count (PROPERTY); SAscore (0-10, higher=harder), RAscore (0-1) (SYNTHESIZABILITY). ANTI-CIRCULARITY: features are discovered/selected on the train split only; tax and steerability are measured on held-out test generations. ORACLE VALIDATION as a primary result, not a footnote: on 3,000 stratified molecules run AiZynthFinder; require route-found rate and route length to track SAscore/RAscore (Spearman |rho|>=0.5) before any strong claim; report route-found rate as the ground-truth synthesizability signal alongside the cheap oracles throughout.

Experiment 1 (C1 - systematic, not random, and not generic drift): For 30-50 property-steering features (top by train-split property-probe AUROC), each (feature,alpha,seed) generates 500 valid molecules; measure target-property gain and Delta-SAscore/Delta-route-found vs alpha=0. DRIFT CONTROLS (all matched to the property-steering KL at each alpha): (a) random-direction, (b) matched non-property SAE feature, (c) non-interpretable raw-latent steering (PCA/difference-of-means on activations), (d) decoding-temperature perturbation. Decisive metric FIRST: per-property NORMALIZED tax slope beta* = d(z-scored SAscore)/d(z-scored target-property), from a mixed-effects model with random slopes over features/seeds, computed per property then pooled. Decision band (pre-set): pooled beta* >= +0.30 (95% CI excludes 0) AND same-sign for >=80% of features AND exceeding every KL-matched control by >=2x => systematic tax confirmed; beta* in [-0.10,+0.10] or CI crossing 0 => not established; beta* <= -0.10 => steering is synthesizability-SAFE (clean counter-result).

Experiment 2 (C2 - blind spot): Using Experiment-1 generations, test whether the cheap checks a practitioner runs reveal 'synthesizability cliffs' (RAscore crossing below 0.5, SAscore jump >=1.0, or route lost). Detectors: RDKit validity, property-predictor confidence, generation log-likelihood. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between each check and the true SAscore/route drop. Decision band: |rho|<=0.20 for validity and property-confidence => blind spot confirmed; (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; >=0.40 => not a blind spot.

Experiment 3 (C3 - decodable but no robust steerable direction): Data: 20,000 held-out molecules labeled by SAscore/RAscore and logP/QED. (a) DECODABILITY: ridge probe (5-fold CV) for each target from SAE features and raw activations (R^2/AUROC). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: best synthesizability direction (probe-weight, difference-of-means high-vs-low, activation-patching from synthesizable runs) vs best logP and QED directions; steer each and measure on-target effect (Cohen's d of oracle value at the alpha maximizing on-target change within the validity budget). SCAFFOLD HELD FIXED operationalized: condition generation on a fixed Bemis-Murcko scaffold prefix (prompt the SMILES with the scaffold tokens), steer only the completion, and compare steered vs unsteered completions of the SAME scaffold (paired). Decisive metric FIRST: steerability ratio r = d(synthesizability)/median(d(logP),d(QED)) at matched decodability. Decision band: probe R^2>=0.50 AND r<=0.33 across >=2/3 direction types => C3 confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial; r>=0.67 with a working direction => synthesizability IS steerable (refutes C3, equally publishable).

Experiment 4 (mitigation, with a pre-set bar): orthogonalize each property-steering vector against the best (weak) synthesizability direction; SUCCESS iff it removes >=50% of the tax (beta* reduction) while retaining >=80% of the on-target property gain. Failure modes reported: if no usable synthesizability direction exists, orthogonalization is undefined and we say so.

ABLATIONS (PRIMARY, not optional): SMILES vs SELFIES, alternative SAE layer, SAE sparsity/width, model size (6M/15M/40M), oracle choice. A finding 'counts' only where it holds on >=2 axes. DELIVERABLE: release the labeled steered-generation set, the audit code (property-vs-synthesizability tradeoff + cliff detector), and per-property tax slopes as a reusable benchmark.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) SAscore/RAscore are in-silico proxies; we now elevate AiZynthFinder route-found rate/route length to a PRIMARY signal on stratified subsets and gate strong claims on cheap-vs-planner agreement. Claims concern model-internal, planner-verified manufacturability, not wet-lab synthesis. 2) C3 is scoped as an absence-under-tested-interventions claim, not a universal one; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types, sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that PROPERTY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable synthesizability handle is equally publishable and directly useful. 3) The tax could be generic off-distribution drift; we use random, matched-non-property, non-interpretable-latent, KL-matched, and temperature controls, requiring the tax to exceed all KL-matched controls. 4) SAE quality/layer could confound Location and the tax; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, sparsity/width, and difference-of-means baselines as primary ablations. 5) Feature selection could induce circularity; we separate feature discovery (train split) from tax/steerability evaluation (test split). 6) Property targets are heterogeneous; we use per-property normalized (z-scored) tax slopes rather than a single raw threshold. 7) An internal synthesizability probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (decodable-but-not-steerable) and the audit/mitigation payoff are the contributions. 8) A null tax is a valuable positive result: it certifies interpretable steering as synthesizability-safe and gives practitioners a clear go-ahead.

Name: regulatory_grammar_syntax_steering
Title: Motifs Without Grammar: Do Genomic Language Models Causally Steer Cis-Regulatory Syntax, or Just Sprinkle Motifs?
Short Hypothesis: We make three typed, separable claims. (Finding) Genomic language models (Evo 2 / regLM-style) possess interpretable, causally-steerable features for the PRESENCE of transcription-factor motifs. (Mechanism) They do NOT possess a robust steerable direction for motif SYNTAX — the inter-motif spacing, strand orientation, and helical-phasing constraints that make a cis-regulatory element functional; syntax is DECODABLE from activations but, under every intervention family we test, weakly steerable (we scope this as 'no robust steerable syntax direction found,' not universal absence). (Audit) Because content-based validity/activity checks look only at motif identity, steering to 'add motif X' silently places motifs in syntactically invalid configurations that break predicted activity, and an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags these silent failures better than output-side checks.
Related Work: Genomic interpretability is active but confined to motif PRESENCE. Per-claim positioning with deltas: (i) SAE motif-feature work (Evo 2 SAEs 2025; small gene-LM SAEs 2025) discovers presence features and shows single-property steering — delta: we ask the orthogonal question of whether SYNTAX, not content, is a steerable handle. (ii) ARGMINN (2024) reads motif spacing preferences from a bespoke predictive architecture — delta: reading syntax from weights is not evidence a general gLM CAUSALLY controls syntax during generation; we test the intervention, not the read-out. (iii) regLM (2024) and DREAM (2024) steer CREs toward target activity/cell-type via LMs + supervised scorers — delta: they optimize scalar activity and never separate the content vs syntax controllability axis. Benchmark critiques (DART-Eval 2024; gLM representational-power 2024; Karollus 2022, models ignoring distal enhancers) hint gLMs capture correlational content over causal grammar but never test this at feature-steering controllability. Setting novelty: promoter/proximal-enhancer syntax is a distinct controllability regime because function there depends on cooperative TF spacing/phasing rather than on any single motif's presence, so content-steering can succeed on its own metric while destroying function — a failure mode absent from prior single-property CRE steering. Our contributions are thus three separable items: a new empirical finding (presence steerable), a mechanistic diagnosis (syntax decodable-but-not-steerable), and an internal audit method — not a new generator.
Abstract: The function of a cis-regulatory element is determined not just by which transcription-factor (TF) motifs it contains, but by their SYNTAX: the spacing, orientation, and helical phasing that let bound proteins cooperate. Interpretability-guided DNA design increasingly steers genomic language model (gLM) features to insert desired motifs, judged by whether the motif appears and predicted activity rises. We surface a phenomenon we call the syntax blind spot: steering an interpretable feature to add a motif reliably increases motif content but places motifs in syntactically incoherent configurations that activity models score as non-functional — and content-based checks never notice. We make three typed claims: (finding) motif PRESENCE is a causally-steerable feature; (mechanism) motif SYNTAX is decodable yet has no robust steerable direction under the interventions we test, unlike presence; (audit) an intervention-free internal syntax-consistency signal flags silently-broken designs better than output-side checks. Using an open gLM (Evo 2 / a regLM-style autoregressive model) with sparse autoencoders and cheap in-silico oracles (FIMO/JASPAR for content; spacing/orientation/10.5-bp phasing statistics for syntax; a supervised sequence-to-activity model for function), we (1) LOCATE presence and syntax features and VALIDATE that content and syntax are separable in probe space before any causal claim; (2) CAUSALLY test whether steering each controls its intended axis with matched-length/GC, shuffled-feature, and raw-hidden-state controls plus a power analysis for the null; (3) quantify the syntax tax content-steering incurs on activity; and (4) audit reliability. Either outcome is actionable: steerable syntax gives grammar-aware design knobs; non-steerable syntax means design tools need explicit grammar constraints and audit layers before wet-lab validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: (primary) a regLM-style autoregressive gLM, ~10M params, trained on the Vaishnav 2022 yeast random-promoter GPRA library (~20M sequences; 1M subsample, one GPU); (cross-model) Evo 2 (7B, public) FROZEN at its published biologically-relevant layer (~26). Base models FROZEN; only BatchTopK SAEs trained (expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2). OPERATIONAL SYNTAX DEFINITION: for an ordered motif pair (A,B), syntax = the tuple (inter-motif gap in bp, relative strand orientation, helical phase = gap mod 10.5). CONTENT oracle: FIMO/JASPAR PWM calls (identity+position); to handle FIMO false positives we require q<0.05 AND confirm with a second caller (HMMER/MOODS) and count a motif present only on agreement. FUNCTION oracle: the GPRA-trained CNN (yeast) plus Enformer (human) as an ORTHOGONAL second function oracle; claims restricted to where the two agree in rank (Spearman>=0.5). Validity gate: GC bounds + pseudo-perplexity. Data: 50,000 held-out promoters for feature-property linking; 5,000 DISSOCIATION PAIRS with identical motif content but functional vs scrambled spacing. Steering = add alpha*d_hat at the SAE layer; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8} residual-RMS units.

Experiment 0 (disentanglement validation, PREREQUISITE): before any causal claim, verify content and syntax are separable in probe space — train probes for motif identity and for the syntax tuple on the dissociation pairs; require content-probe AUROC>=0.8 with near-chance syntax leakage and syntax-probe AUROC>=0.7 with near-chance content leakage (cross-prediction AUROC<=0.6). If not separable for a motif combination, that combination is excluded and reported.

Experiment 1 (finding - PRESENCE is causally steerable): identify presence features (held-out probe AUROC>=0.8), steer to ADD a target motif to sequences lacking it; 500 sequences per (feature,alpha,seed) for the 15 most frequent JASPAR yeast motifs. Controls: random-direction, shuffled-feature, matched-length and matched-GC. Decisive metric FIRST: two-caller motif-installation rate. Decision band: >=0.60 AND >=0.40 above best control for >=2/3 motifs => presence is a handle; gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; <0.15 => not steerable (undercuts premise, reported).

Experiment 2 (mechanism - SYNTAX decodable but not steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe SAE features/raw activations for the syntax tuple, controlling for content (report AUROC/R^2). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head with a FORMAL objective: shift inter-motif gap toward a target helical phase (e.g. 5 bp -> 21 bp) while holding content fixed, using best syntax direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means functional-vs-scrambled, activation-patching from correct-syntax), compared against raw-hidden-state directions and NULL syntax features. Decisive metric FIRST: efficacy ratio r = (normalized achieved gap shift)/(presence-installation efficacy). POWER: pre-compute the N of generations needed to detect r=0.5 at 80% power; report the achieved MDE so the null is statistically supported. Decision band: syntax decodable (AUROC>=0.70) AND r<=0.33 (CI upper bound below 0.33) => mechanism confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial; r>=0.67 => syntax IS steerable (refutes, equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (audit part A - silent breakage): steer presence features, 500 sequences per level. Among content-satisfying, valid, low-perplexity sequences, measure activity loss from bad syntax. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-BREAKAGE RATE = fraction below the 10th percentile of natural-CRE activity despite passing content+validity; plus Spearman rho between cheap checks (content-satisfaction, perplexity) and true activity. Decision band: breakage>=0.30 AND |rho|<=0.20 => silent blind spot confirmed; [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; <0.10 or |rho|>=0.40 => not silent.

Experiment 4 (audit part B - internal flag): no-intervention score = syntax-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC for detecting eventually-non-functional sequences from Exp 3, vs output-side detectors (content-satisfaction, perplexity, function-oracle confidence). Decision band: internal AUROC>=0.75 AND >=0.10 above best output-side => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; <=0.05 => internal signal no better (reported; mechanism diagnosis still stands). ROBUSTNESS: Evo 2 vs regLM, promoter vs proximal-enhancer; counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Function and syntax are assessed by in-silico oracles (GPRA CNN, Enformer, FIMO/JASPAR); these are proxies, so claims concern model-internal, in-silico-verified syntactic controllability, NOT biological truth about regulatory grammar — stated explicitly. Sequence-to-activity models capture promoters better than distal enhancers (Karollus 2022), so core claims are on promoter/proximal-enhancer regimes and enhancer results are reported separately. We use two function oracles and two motif callers and restrict claims to where they agree. 2) The syntax-non-steerability claim is scoped as absence-under-tested-interventions; we mitigate with multiple intervention types, strength sweeps, a power analysis / reported MDE, and head-to-head calibration that PRESENCE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable-syntax result is equally publishable and valuable for grammar-aware design. 3) Content and syntax may be entangled for some motif combinations; Experiment 0 validates separability in probe space and excludes/reports inseparable cases. 4) SAE quality/layer could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, the Evo 2 published layer, raw-activation probes, shuffled-feature and null-feature controls. 5) An internal syntax probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis and audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 6) If no syntax tax is found (content steering preserves grammar/activity), that is a valuable positive result establishing gLM feature-steering as grammar-safe for regulatory DNA design.

Name: rna_folding_mirage_steering
Title: The Folding Mirage: Do Interpretable Features Control an RNA's Local Motifs While Silently Breaking Its Global Thermodynamic Fold?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of RNA language models afford causal, steerable control over LOCAL structural motifs (a hairpin, a stem, a poly-U tract), but NOT over the GLOBAL thermodynamic fold that defines RNA function. Consequently, steering a feature to insert a desired local structure silently produces sequences whose true minimum-free-energy fold and target-structure Boltzmann probability collapse — a 'folding mirage' — that motif-content and validity checks miss, but which an intervention-free internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags. We do NOT propose steering itself (SAE-RNA already reports it); our claim is that local-motif steerability and global-fold steerability DECOUPLE, that the decoupling exceeds matched controls, and that the resulting mirage is auditable. The global-non-steerability part is scoped as 'no robust steerable global-fold direction found under tested interventions,' not universal absence.
Related Work: Positioning across four rows with per-row deltas. (i) Descriptive RNA-LM interpretability (SAE-RNA 2025; SPIRAL/BiRNA-BERT 2026; small gene-LM SAEs 2025) finds features for stems, hairpins, poly-tracts, ncRNA families — delta: descriptive only, no test of whether steering preserves the global fold. (ii) Steerability: SAE-RNA reports single-property steering — delta: we do not claim steering as novel; we test the local-vs-global CONTRAST and its reliability. (iii) Inverse folding / RNA design LMs (RNAinformer 2024; 'Designing RNAs with Language Models' 2026; AIDO.RNA 2025) hit target secondary structures via supervised/RL — delta: no interpretability, no feature-level steering, no audit of silent failure. (iv) Oracle-based steering-audit work in protein/molecule (InterPLM, ProtSAE) establishes the content-vs-global-property axis — delta: never applied to RNA, where the global functional property has an EXACT physics oracle. RNA is the ideal testbed because ViennaRNA computes the exact MFE structure, ensemble free energy, and Boltzmann probability of any target structure instantly and free, turning 'silent global failure' from a proxy into a computable quantity. Novelty is explicitly threefold: the empirical FINDING (local/global decoupling), the oracle-grounded evaluation SETTING (ViennaRNA as clean ground truth for steering reliability), and the intervention-free AUDIT mechanism. This is the first interpretability-of-generation study for RNA to contrast local-motif against global-fold steerability and to surface the folding-mirage phenomenon.
Abstract: An RNA's function is set by its global thermodynamic fold, not merely by which local motifs it contains: the same hairpin can sit in a functional structure or be buried in a completely different minimum-free-energy conformation. Interpretability-guided design increasingly steers language-model features to add desired structural elements, judged by whether the motif appears. We surface a phenomenon we call the folding mirage: steering an interpretable feature to insert a local structure (a hairpin, a stem) reliably increases that motif's presence but drives the sequence's true global fold — its MFE structure and the Boltzmann probability of the intended target — to collapse, invisible to motif-content and validity checks. We stress we do not propose steering itself; our claim is that local-motif and global-fold steerability DECOUPLE beyond matched controls, and that the mirage is auditable. We then ask: do RNA-LMs represent the global fold as a compact, causally-steerable feature the way they represent local motifs, or is global consistency emergent and weakly steerable? RNA is the ideal testbed because ViennaRNA gives the exact global fold, ensemble free energy, and target-structure Boltzmann probability for free. Using RiNALMo/RNA-FM with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE local-motif and global-fold features under pre-registered operational criteria; (2) CAUSALLY test each with hard controls (scrambled-feature, matched-activation, intervention-size matching) plus a specificity negative control; (3) quantify the mirage — the drop in target-structure Boltzmann probability that local steering incurs; and (4) AUDIT whether an internal thermodynamic-consistency signal flags mirages better than motif-content or likelihood. Either outcome matters: a mirage means RNA design evaluation must add global-fold checks; a null certifies feature-steering as thermodynamically safe.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (public, FROZEN): RiNALMo (650M) and RNA-FM (~100M); as encoders, generation is by masked infilling. Only SAEs trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered latents ranked by importance, the antibody-SAE recipe recovering steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, cheap): ViennaRNA — RNAfold MFE structure/energy, partition function for ensemble free energy, and the Boltzmann probability that a sequence folds into a specified TARGET (primary GLOBAL signal). LOCAL oracle: presence/position of a hairpin loop / stem / poly-U tract from the predicted structure. OPERATIONAL FEATURE CRITERIA (pre-registered, set before main experiments): a LOCAL-motif feature must have held-out probe AUROC>=0.8 for one specific motif AND near-chance AUROC for global-fold class; a GLOBAL-fold feature must predict MFE-per-nt / ensemble free energy (R^2>=0.40) AND not be explainable by any single local motif. PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY ENDPOINT per experiment stated below (no metric shopping). Validity gate: GC bounds + pseudo-perplexity. Data: 20,000 held-out Rfam ncRNA spanning tRNA-scale (~76 nt) and longer families for feature-property linking; 5,000 DISSOCIATION PAIRS (same local hairpin in well-folded vs misfolded global context). Steering = add alpha*d_hat during masked infilling; alpha in {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-motif features are causally steerable): steer local-motif features to INSERT a target motif; 500 infilled sequences per (feature,alpha,seed). Controls: random-direction, scrambled-feature, matched-activation-norm. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: local-motif installation rate (target motif in the RNAfold structure). Decision band: >=0.60 AND >=0.40 over best control for >=2/3 motifs => local control genuine; gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; <0.15 => not steerable (premise fails, reported).

Experiment 2 (H2 - global fold decodable but not steerable): (a) DECODABILITY: probe for global properties (MFE/nt, ensemble free energy, base-pairing fraction, fold class) controlling for local content; AUROC/R^2. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head with intervention-SIZE matched to Experiment 1: steer best global-fold direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means well-vs-misfolded, activation-patching from correctly-folded) to RAISE target-structure Boltzmann probability while holding local content fixed. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: ratio r = global-fold efficacy / local efficacy (Exp 1). Decision band: global decodable (R^2>=0.40 or AUROC>=0.70) AND r<=0.33 => H2 confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test whether Ordered SAEs raise it); r>=0.67 => global fold IS steerable (refutes, equally publishable).

Experiment 2b (SPECIFICITY negative control): steer local-motif features on sequences where the target motif is thermodynamically compatible with the existing fold (small, peripheral); here local steering should NOT collapse the global fold. Confirms the mirage in Exp 3 is a genuine decoupling, not an artifact of any perturbation breaking folds.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the folding mirage): steer local-motif features, 500 sequences per level. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: SILENT-MISFOLD RATE = fraction of local-motif-satisfying, valid sequences with target-structure Boltzmann probability <0.10; plus mirage slope d(Boltzmann)/d(local gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (motif-content, perplexity) and true global health. Decision band: misfold>=0.30 AND |rho|<=0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; <0.10 or |rho|>=0.40 => no silent mirage (steering thermodynamically safe, positive result). The mirage is declared a NEW phenomenon only if the decoupling exceeds every matched control AND the specificity control (2b) is negative.

Experiment 4 (H4 - intervention-free thermodynamic-consistency flag): no-intervention score = global-fold-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. PRIMARY ENDPOINT: AUROC detecting misfolded (low-Boltzmann) sequences from Exp 3, vs output-side (motif content, perplexity, likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC>=0.75 AND >=0.10 over best output-side => flag confirmed; (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; <=0.05 => no better (reported). APPLICATION SCENARIO tied to the audit: in a batch of steered tRNA-scaffold designs, the flag should let a designer discard mirages before ordering/synthesis, avoiding wasted wet-lab cost. ABLATIONS (primary): layer choice, sequence length (short vs longer), target motif class, steering strength calibration, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, RiNALMo vs RNA-FM. Corroborate a subset with a structure-aware model (ERNIE-RNA/structRFM). A finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Global fold is assessed by ViennaRNA (nearest-neighbor thermodynamic model), well-validated but in-silico; it ignores tertiary interactions/pseudoknots and cellular context, so claims concern thermodynamic-model-verified SECONDARY-structure global folding, NOT wet-lab or tertiary function — stated explicitly. We corroborate a subset with a structure-aware model and report agreement. 2) The global-non-steerability claim is scoped as absence-under-tested-interventions; we mitigate with multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), strength sweeps, and head-to-head calibration that LOCAL features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — a null is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive steerable global-fold handle is equally publishable and useful for structure-aware design. 3) The mirage could be generic off-distribution drift; controlled with random-direction, scrambled-feature, matched-activation controls, a specificity negative control (Exp 2b), and by testing motif-specific displacement. 4) Local and global structure are partly entangled (a large motif dominates the fold); the dissociation pairs separate them and we report where separation is impossible. 5) SAE quality/layer could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal consistency probe might not beat a raw-activation probe on AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (local-decodable, global-weakly-steerable) and audit payoff remain the contributions. 7) A null mirage is a valuable positive result establishing RNA-LM feature-steering as thermodynamically safe, directly reassuring RNA design and synthetic-biology practitioners.

Name: conservation_law_mirage_reactions
Title: Balanced by Habit, Not by Law: Do Reaction Generative Models Internally Represent Mass Conservation as a Steerable Feature, or Fake It?
Short Hypothesis: We advance three separable, typed claims. (C1, phenomenon) Autoregressive reaction-prediction models emit atom-balanced reactions (matching element counts across the arrow) not because they hold a compact, causally-steerable internal representation of the conservation LAW, but via a shallow atom-copying heuristic tied to local token context; steering an interpretable feature to alter a product's chemistry (add/remove an atom or functional group) therefore silently breaks mass balance—a 'conservation mirage' that ordinary SMILES-validity checks miss. (C2, mechanism) Mass/atom conservation is linearly DECODABLE from activations yet, under every intervention family we test, has no robust steerable direction the way local chemistry features do—a decodable-but-weakly-steerable GLOBAL invariant, scoped as 'no robust steerable balance direction found under tested interventions,' not universal absence. (C3, audit) An intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags mirage reactions better than validity or model likelihood. The broader lesson we test: in generative models a global conservation invariant can be behaviorally satisfied without being a steerable internal object, even while LOCAL properties are cleanly steerable.
Related Work: FlowER (2025) and atom-conserving CRNNs (2023) show data-driven reaction models routinely VIOLATE mass/atom conservation, producing 'hallucinatory' unbalanced reactions, and fix this ARCHITECTURALLY by hard-coding electron/atom-balance layers—treating conservation as an external constraint, never asking whether a standard model internally represents it. 'Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' (2025) finds molecular transformers implement ring/branch SYNTAX circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and 'Physics Steering' (2025) shows physics foundation models have steerable concept directions—but neither studies reactions or the conservation invariant, and neither asks whether a global conservation law (as opposed to a local property) is a steerable handle. Conservation-law discovery work (Noether-from-DNN 2021; stoichiometry-nullspace methods 2014/2024) extracts laws from PREDICTIVE dynamics models, never from a generative reaction LM's internal features, and never tests steering reliability. No prior work (a) asks whether a generative reaction model represents mass/atom conservation as a causal, steerable feature, (b) surfaces the conservation-mirage phenomenon where chemistry-steering silently unbalances a reaction, or (c) provides an internal balance-reliability audit. This introduces the content-vs-conservation-law axis into interpretability-of-generation for chemical reactions—a new object class where conservation is an exact, instantly computable oracle (element-count matching / stoichiometry null space)—distinct from all prior single-property steering and from all architectural conservation fixes. Positioning as a three-row contrast with explicit deltas: (i) architectural conservation-enforcement (FlowER 2025; atom-conserving CRNNs 2023) CHANGES the model to force balance—we FREEZE the model and ask whether balance is an internal steerable law; (ii) local feature-steering (Circuits/Features/Heuristics 2025; Physics Steering 2025) steers a LOCAL property and never audits a global invariant's side-effect nor tests the invariant's own steerability; (iii) conservation-law discovery (Noether-from-DNN 2021; stoichiometry-nullspace 2014/2024) extracts laws from PREDICTIVE dynamics models, not a generative reaction LM's features. A non-obvious setting distinction: a global stoichiometric invariant in sequence generation is qualitatively unlike local property steering because it is a conserved relation between the reactant and product SIDES that no single local edit satisfies in isolation, so local steerability gives no reason to expect the global law is steerable. Contributions are threefold and typed—empirical phenomenon (C1, the mirage), mechanistic diagnosis (C3, heuristic-not-law), and a released element-residual balance-audit benchmark plus detector reusable across reaction generators—not a new reaction-prediction method.
Abstract: Mass conservation is chemistry's most basic law: a valid reaction has identical element counts on both sides. Data-driven reaction models are known to hallucinate unbalanced reactions, and the field fixes this by hard-coding balance into the architecture—never asking whether a standard model represents conservation internally. We surface a phenomenon we call the conservation mirage and make three typed claims. (C1) An autoregressive reaction transformer emits mostly balanced reactions via a shallow atom-copying heuristic, not a genuine internal law: steering an interpretable feature to change a product's chemistry (add a methyl, swap a halogen, remove an oxygen) reliably changes the chemistry but silently breaks atom balance, invisible to SMILES-validity checks and evident only from element counting. (C2) Conservation is linearly decodable from activations yet, under every intervention family we test, has no robust steerable direction the way local chemistry features do—a decodable-but-weakly-steerable global invariant. (C3) A cheap intervention-free balance-consistency signal flags mirage reactions better than validity or likelihood. Reactions are the ideal testbed because balance is an exact, free oracle (element-count vectors and the stoichiometry null space). We quantify how often validity-only screening would pass unbalanced outputs and translate it into wasted effort for retrosynthesis filtering, reaction editing, and autonomous-discovery loops. Either outcome is actionable: a real mirage changes how steered reactions are screened; a null certifies steering as conservation-safe. We release an open balance-audit benchmark and detector, and test the broader lesson that a global invariant can be non-steerable even where local properties are steerable.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Model: an autoregressive reaction transformer (Molecular-Transformer-style, ~30M params) trained on USPTO-MIT reaction SMILES (479,035 reactions), filtered to the atom-balanced subset with atom-mapping retained; FROZEN after training. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability that TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen mid layer, seeds 0/1/2. Oracle (exact, free via RDKit): the reactant-minus-product element-count residual - a reaction is atom-balanced iff the residual is the zero vector (charge balance and atom-mapping completeness also computed). LOCAL-CHEMISTRY oracle: presence/absence of specified product functional groups/atoms via SMARTS. Validity gate: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid on both sides. BASELINE (needed for the absence claim): confirm the frozen model natively emits atom-balanced products at rate >= 0.80 on held-out reactants, well above a token-shuffle chance rate; if it does not, the mechanism claim is reframed. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during product decoding given fixed reactants; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - local-chemistry features are causally steerable): Identify chemistry features (fire when a product contains a given functional group/atom; probe AUROC >= 0.8) and steer to add/remove that group in the product given fixed reactants. Generate 500 completions per (feature, alpha, seed). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: chemistry-installation rate (intended group/atom change appears in the product). Decision band: rate >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of groups => chemistry control genuine (H1 holds); gain [0.15,0.40) => inconclusive; gain < 0.15 => chemistry not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the conservation mirage: chemistry steering silently breaks mass balance; SMILES-validity checks miss it): Steer chemistry features and generate 500 completions per level. Decisive metric FIRST: SILENT-IMBALANCE RATE = fraction of chemistry-satisfying, SMILES-valid reactions whose element-count residual is nonzero, plus the mirage slope d(|residual|)/d(chemistry gain) and Spearman rho between cheap checks (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity) and true balance. Decision band: imbalance rate >= 0.30 AND |rho| <= 0.20 => mirage + blind spot confirmed; imbalance [0.10,0.30) or |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; imbalance < 0.10 or |rho| >= 0.40 => steering is conservation-safe (positive result).

Experiment 3 (H3 - conservation is decodable-but-not-steerable and rests on a shallow atom-copying heuristic, not a compact conservation-LAW feature): (a) DECODABILITY: probe 'is-balanced' / the element residual from activations, reporting AUROC and the earliest product-decoding position at which balance status is decodable. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best conservation direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means balanced-vs-unbalanced, activation-patching from balanced runs) to RESTORE balance (drive residual->0) while holding product chemistry fixed; ratio r = conservation efficacy / chemistry efficacy from Experiment 1. (c) MECHANISM (heuristic vs law): using the 4,000 controlled pairs that hold the same product functional group in balanced vs deliberately unbalanced reactions, test whether the located 'conservation' unit tracks the GLOBAL residual (law) or LOCAL product content (heuristic). Decisive metric FIRST: r, read together with the mechanism contrast. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND the unit predicts local content (AUROC >= 0.80) but the global residual only at <= 0.60 => H3 confirmed (inert + shallow heuristic); r in (0.33,0.67) or residual-AUROC in (0.60,0.75) => partial; r >= 0.67 => a genuine steerable conservation handle exists, refuting H3.

Experiment 4 (H4 - an intervention-free internal balance-consistency signal flags the mirage): No-intervention score = conservation-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the mass-unbalanced reactions from Experiment 2. Systems: internal signal vs output-side (SMILES-validity, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, forward-prediction vs retrosynthesis framing; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DEFINITIONS (set before results). A 'compact steerable feature' = a single SAE latent (or a <=3-dim difference-of-means direction) whose steering yields on-target efficacy (Cohen's d) >= the chemistry features' median at matched activation-norm and matched KL; 'decodable' = probe AUROC >= 0.75. The internal BALANCE-AUDIT SIGNAL is defined mathematically: s = sigmoid(w . h_t + b), a logistic probe on the mid-layer residual h_t predicting zero element-residual, trained on the TRAIN split only and frozen; evaluation uses held-out TEST generations, split 80/10/10 by reaction scaffold to prevent leakage. Pseudo-perplexity here = mean per-token negative log-likelihood of the generated product conditioned on the reactants (left-to-right)—the same quantity a practitioner reads off the model—making it a fair output-side comparator.

NON-SAE BASELINES (so a null is not blamed on the SAE): (i) raw-activation linear representation editing (difference-of-means / logistic-probe direction on the un-decomposed residual stream); (ii) a decoder-logit balance constraint (down-weight product tokens that increase |element residual|). Both run head-to-head with SAE steering in Experiments 1 and 3. CAUSAL ATOM-SOURCE control: test whether steering changes atom-source alignment/copy patterns (attention-to-reactant-atom maps), not just final element residuals, supporting the atom-copying-heuristic claim.

EXPERIMENT 5 (incremental-insight sanity): compare the internal diagnosis against an explicit balance-aware constrained-decoding baseline (reject/repair products whose running element residual cannot reach zero). Report whether the internal audit adds information beyond this trivial output check—specifically whether it flags mirages EARLIER in decoding (earliest-reliable-detection position) and at lower compute. STAKES ESTIMATE: on a fixed 5,000-reaction steered set, report the fraction of SMILES-valid outputs that are mass-unbalanced (the rate at which validity-only screening passes unusable reactions) and translate it into wasted-effort terms for retrosynthesis proposal filtering, reaction editing, and autonomous-discovery loops.

ADDED ROBUSTNESS: a second dataset (USPTO-50k / Open Reaction Database temporal split) and a second tokenization (SELFIES) show the phenomenon is not a USPTO-MIT or SMILES artifact; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Mass/atom balance is an EXACT, non-proxy oracle (element counting is deterministic), which is a strength; the main proxy is downstream 'feasibility', which we deliberately do not claim—core claims concern the objectively-computable conservation invariant, not reaction viability. 2) The conservation-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that CHEMISTRY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null conservation result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable conservation handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for building balance-aware reaction models without architectural surgery. 3) The mirage could be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; we use random-direction and matched-non-chemistry-feature controls and test whether the mirage tracks chemistry-specific displacement. 4) Chemistry and balance are partly entangled (a chemistry edit that adds an atom must be sourced from a reactant); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) and the atom-source diagnostics are designed to separate 'model knows the atom must come from somewhere' from 'model copies atoms locally', and we report where separation is impossible. 5) Some USPTO reactions are themselves unbalanced/incompletely recorded; we filter to a curated balanced-reaction training/eval subset and report label quality. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 7) An internal balance probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (chemistry-decodable, conservation-weakly-steerable, heuristic-vs-law) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 8) If no mirage is found (chemistry steering preserves balance), that is a valuable positive result establishing that reaction-model feature steering is conservation-safe and that the model represents conservation robustly.

Name: kinetic_thermodynamic_steering_gap
Title: Steer the Endpoint, Not the Path: Do Interpretable Features Control Thermodynamic but Not Kinetic Properties of Generated Molecules?
Short Hypothesis: We make one primary, typed claim and one audit claim. (Primary phenomenon—an endpoint-vs-pathway controllability gap) Interpretable SAE features of molecular/protein generators trained on STATIC endpoints afford causal, steerable control over THERMODYNAMIC/equilibrium properties (stability, binding affinity, solubility, fold free energy) but NOT over KINETIC properties (transition-state barriers, folding rates, metastability, dissociation kinetics): steering toward a kinetic target silently shifts the thermodynamic ENDPOINT instead, a 'kinetics blind spot,' because pathways/barriers are absent from endpoint-only training. Kinetic control is scoped as decodable-but-weakly-steerable under tested interventions, not universally absent. (Audit) An intervention-free internal kinetic-consistency signal flags these silently-uncontrolled designs better than equilibrium-property checks. The general principle we test: dynamical/pathway controllability of a generator is contingent on dynamics-bearing training data, so endpoint checks can certify a design that is kinetically invalid.
Related Work: Two threads meet for the first time. (1) 'Physics Steering' (2025) shows a PHYSICS foundation model (trained directly on simulation trajectories) has causally-steerable directions for dynamical concepts like diffusion speed and temporal progression; Latent Thermodynamic Flows (2025), Thermodynamic Interpolation (2025), and tLaSDI (2024) build generative models that capture temperature/kinetics but do so by INJECTING thermodynamic structure or training on dynamics data. (2) Molecular/protein interpretability-of-generation (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Circuits/Features/Heuristics in Molecular Transformers 2025) discovers and steers features for endpoint/equilibrium properties and never touches kinetics. Crucially, the physics-FM result raises the sharp question: does a generator trained ONLY on static molecules/sequences (no trajectories, no barriers) also learn steerable dynamical/kinetic handles, or is dynamical controllability contingent on dynamics-bearing training data? No prior work (a) contrasts kinetic vs thermodynamic steerability in molecular/protein generators, (b) surfaces the kinetics-blind-spot phenomenon where kinetic steering collapses to endpoint change, or (c) audits when a generator's kinetic-property claim is trustworthy. This introduces the endpoint-vs-pathway axis into interpretability-of-generation, distinct from all my prior proposals (folding fold, symmetry, conservation, synthesizability, syntax) which concern static structural facts, not dynamical/pathway properties. Contrast of prior families (closest-baseline delta in the last row): [endpoint steering] InterPLM/ProtSAE/chemistry-LM SAEs—steer equilibrium properties, never kinetics; [dynamics-trained generators] Latent Thermodynamic Flows/Thermodynamic Interpolation/tLaSDI—capture kinetics by INJECTING dynamics or training on trajectories; [physics-FM trajectory steering] Physics Steering—steerable dynamical directions BUT the model is trained on simulation trajectories; [THIS proposal] a static-endpoint-trained generator with SAE steering, asking whether a kinetic handle exists WITHOUT dynamics-bearing training data. The precise delta from the closest baseline: static-trained SAE steering, not trajectory-trained dynamical steering. Novelty locus is a FINDING (an endpoint-vs-pathway controllability gap) plus an evaluation PRINCIPLE, not a new theory of kinetics. Who cares: molecular design (barrier-aware generation), protein engineering (folding-rate/off-rate design), and mechanistic interpretability (what dynamical structure static training can and cannot induce); in practice they would add pathway-aware checks and stop trusting endpoint-only steering for kinetic targets.
Abstract: A molecule's usefulness often depends on kinetics, not just thermodynamics: a metastable polymorph, a slow-off-rate binder, a fast-folding protein, or a low-barrier catalyst are defined by PATHWAYS and BARRIERS, not equilibrium endpoints. Generative models for molecules and proteins are trained almost entirely on static endpoints, yet interpretability-guided design increasingly steers their features to hit target properties. Our one primary, falsifiable claim is an endpoint-vs-pathway controllability gap: interpretable features causally control THERMODYNAMIC properties but not KINETIC ones, so steering toward a kinetic target silently shifts the thermodynamic ENDPOINT instead—a 'kinetics blind spot' invisible to equilibrium and validity checks. The strongest so-what: endpoint checks can certify a design that is kinetically invalid. Recent work shows a physics model trained on trajectories has steerable dynamical directions; we test the complementary hypothesis that generators trained WITHOUT dynamics lack a causal kinetic handle. Using ESM-2 protein LMs and a SMILES chemical LM with sparse autoencoders, plus cheap kinetic oracles (contact-order folding-rate proxies, ML-interatomic-potential barrier estimates, Langevin mean-first-passage-time) validated on a small higher-fidelity subset, we LOCATE thermodynamic and kinetic features, CAUSALLY contrast endpoint against pathway control with endpoint-matched pairs and randomized-label controls, quantify the blind spot, and AUDIT whether an internal kinetic-consistency signal flags silently-uncontrolled designs before expensive simulation. Concrete uses: slow-off-rate binders, folding-rate design, barrier-aware molecule generation. Either way is a general evaluation principle for generative design: a positive kinetic handle is a surprising capability; a null tells designers to add pathway-aware checks and not trust endpoint-only steering.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M) for proteins (generation by masked infilling) and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~15M params) for molecules. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. THERMODYNAMIC/endpoint oracles: protein fold stability (a fine-tuned stability head or FoldX-style dG), GRAVY, DSSP secondary-structure content on ESMFold; molecule logP/QED, solubility proxy. KINETIC/pathway oracles: protein folding-rate proxy from absolute contact order (the Plaxco relation) and a native-state metastability proxy; molecule reaction-barrier estimate via a pretrained ML interatomic potential (climbing-image NEB-lite on fixed reaction templates) and mean-first-passage-time from short Langevin dynamics. Because kinetic oracles are compute-heavier, they are run on a capped 2,000-object subset per level. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules). Data: for calibration, ~52 two-state proteins from a folding-kinetics database (e.g., ACPro/KineticDB) plus a fixed set of reaction templates; first confirm the frozen models natively span a meaningful kinetic RANGE (so absence-of-control is meaningful). Steering = add alpha*d_hat; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - thermodynamic/equilibrium features are causally steerable): Identify thermodynamic features (correlate with stability/logP endpoints; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer toward a target endpoint. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target endpoint effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, at the within-validity-budget alpha). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over random control for >=2/3 of features => thermodynamic control genuine (H1 holds); d over control in [0.2,0.4) => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - kinetics is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and steering a kinetic target silently changes the thermodynamic endpoint instead): (a) DECODABILITY: partial-correlation probe for the kinetic property controlling for the endpoint; report R^2 (low R^2 here is itself consistent with kinetics being absent from static endpoint-only training). (b) STEERABILITY: steer the best candidate kinetic direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means fast-vs-slow, activation-patching, endpoint-orthogonalized direction) toward a kinetic target while holding the endpoint fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: (i) LEAKAGE FRACTION = share of steering displacement landing on the endpoint axis rather than the kinetic axis; (ii) SILENT-KINETIC-FAILURE RATE = fraction of 'kinetically-steered', valid objects whose kinetic property did not move beyond oracle noise (or moved wrong-sign) while an endpoint changed; (iii) ratio r = kinetic efficacy / thermodynamic efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND leakage >= 0.60 AND silent-failure >= 0.30 => kinetics blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) or leakage in (0.40,0.60) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a genuine kinetic handle exists in a static-trained generator, refuting H2 (surprising, equally reportable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - the blind spot is invisible to equilibrium checks but an internal kinetic-consistency signal flags it): (a) INVISIBILITY: Spearman rho between endpoint-property change / pseudo-perplexity and true kinetic change; band |rho| <= 0.20 => equilibrium checks miss it, |rho| >= 0.40 => they catch it. (b) INTERNAL FLAG: a no-intervention score = kinetic-probe confidence / SAE-feature coherence read mid-generation; Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC detecting the silently-uncontrolled designs from Experiment 2 vs output-side signals (endpoint property, validity, likelihood). Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => flag confirmed; margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS & SCALE: both domains, two ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs; test whether kinetic steerability rises with model scale - no rise is consistent with the 'absent from training signal' explanation; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DECISION (blind spot vs no-evidence). 'Kinetics blind spot' is asserted ONLY if (a) the frozen model natively spans a kinetic range AND (b) thermodynamic control is calibrated (Exp 1 passes) AND (c) kinetic efficacy r <= 0.33 with leakage >= 0.60; if (a) or (b) fails we report 'no evidence / uninterpretable,' not a blind spot. OPERATIONAL, DOMAIN-SEPARATED PROPERTY DEFINITIONS (no bundling): proteins—thermodynamic = fold stability dG and DSSP secondary-structure content; kinetic = folding rate (contact-order/Plaxco proxy) and native-state metastability; molecules—thermodynamic = logP/QED/solubility proxy; kinetic = reaction-barrier height (ML-interatomic-potential NEB-lite on fixed templates) and mean-first-passage-time (short Langevin). Each property gets its own probe, direction, and decision band.

ADDED CONTROLS: (i) endpoint-matched pairs (same thermodynamic endpoint, different kinetics) to isolate endpoint-independent kinetic signal; (ii) randomized kinetic-label controls (shuffle kinetic targets) to bound spurious efficacy; (iii) oracle-noise sensitivity (repeat with injected proxy noise; require conclusions stable). STRONGER BASELINES beyond SAE features: random directions, endpoint-orthogonal directions, raw-activation linear probes/edits, and a black-box no-SAE steering baseline (optimize a raw-residual direction). HIGHER-FIDELITY VALIDATION: on a small subset, corroborate barrier proxies with short metadynamics/xTB and folding-rate proxies with literature two-state rates; strong claims restricted to where fidelity tiers agree.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Kinetic properties are assessed by in-silico proxies (contact-order folding-rate predictors, ML-interatomic-potential barrier estimates, short-Langevin MFPT), which are approximations of true kinetics and far cheaper than full MD; we validate proxies against each other and against literature rate data on a subset, and restrict strong claims to cases where proxies agree. Claims concern model-internal, proxy-verified kinetic controllability, not experimental rates - stated explicitly. 2) The kinetic-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, endpoint-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a kinetic range, and head-to-head calibrating that THERMODYNAMIC features ARE steerable in the same pipeline - so a null kinetic result is meaningful rather than a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable kinetic handle in a static-trained generator) is equally publishable and surprising. 3) Kinetics and thermodynamics are partly coupled (Bell-Evans-style barrier-stability correlations); the partial-correlation feature selection and endpoint-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) are designed to isolate genuinely endpoint-independent kinetic signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Kinetic oracles (NEB/Langevin) are compute-heavier than endpoint oracles; we cap simulation on a subset and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal kinetic probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (thermodynamics-decodable-and-steerable, kinetics-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If kinetic steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that static-trained generators encode causal pathway information.

Name: epistasis_steering_blindspot
Title: Levers for Positions, Not for Couplings: Can Interpretable Features Causally Control Epistasis in Protein Language Models?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of protein language models give causal, steerable control over SINGLE-POSITION (additive) sequence properties, but we hypothesize they do NOT give control over EPISTASIS—the context-dependent coupling that makes one position's optimal residue depend on another. No prior work has tested causal steering of epistatic-coupling features in pLM SAEs. We commit to ONE primary hypothesis with ONE fallback: steering a feature to install a desired coupling (a compensatory pair, an allosteric/functional linkage) silently changes additive properties while the intended coupling fails to form—an 'epistasis blind spot' that single-mutant checks miss but a double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes (primary); the fallback is that coupling is only WEAKLY steerable relative to additive control. Whichever holds, the audit contribution stands: an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs, telling engineers to run double-mutant-cycle checks before synthesis. We keep 'scientific phenomenon discovery' (is coupling a steerable object?) separate from 'design utility' (can we make couplings on demand?), so the result is informative even where the wet-lab oracle is imperfect.
Related Work: pLM interpretability/steering work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; antibody-SAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Automated Neuron Labelling 2025; SAEs for low-N design 2025) discovers and steers features that all encode INTRINSIC, single-position or local-motif properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger motifs, thermostability) and evaluate whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a distinct biology literature establishes that pLMs INTERNALLY capture epistasis: ESM-2 stores coevolving-residue statistics like a Markov Random Field (Zhang et al. 2024), pLMs capture both structural-contact and long-range FUNCTIONAL couplings zero-shot (2025), and higher-order epistasis is present in sequence-function models (2024). Crucially, no work connects these: none asks whether the epistatic/coupling structure pLMs demonstrably represent is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever, contrasts coupling-steerability against single-position steerability, or audits when a designer's coupling request silently fails. This distinguishes the proposal from all single-property steering work (which assumes an additive target) and from the epistasis-probing literature (which is purely descriptive/predictive, never touching feature-level steering of generation). Epistasis is the ideal testbed because it has an exact, well-established quantitative oracle — the double-mutant cycle (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) computable from deep mutational scanning (DMS) data or in-silico stability predictors. Compact contrast: [additive-property steering] InterPLM/ProtSAE/Steering-PLMs/antibody-SAE—steer single-position/local-motif traits, evaluate standalone appearance; [descriptive epistasis probing] Zhang 2024 (ESM-2 as MRF), zero-shot coupling capture 2025, higher-order epistasis 2024—show couplings are REPRESENTED but never intervene; [THIS proposal] causal feature-STEERING of couplings, contrasted head-to-head with additive steering and audited. The nearest baselines for coupling control (categorical-Jacobian reads, coevolution statistics) are PREDICTIVE, not generative interventions, so they do not imply steerability. Who would use it: protein designers (compensatory/allosteric design), SAE/interpretability researchers (limits of feature steering), and model-audit practitioners. We keep the scientific question (is coupling a steerable object?) separate from design utility (can couplings be installed on demand?) so the contribution survives an imperfect wet-lab oracle. Deliverable: a coupling-steering audit protocol and a labeled additive-vs-coupling steering benchmark.
Abstract: A protein's function is shaped not only by which residue sits at each position but by epistasis: the coupling that makes the best residue at one position depend on another, underlying compensatory mutations, allosteric linkages, and folding cooperativity. Interpretability-guided design steers language-model features to install properties, and pLMs are known to internally capture epistatic couplings—yet every demonstrated steering target is an additive, single-position property. No prior work has tested causal steering of epistatic-coupling features in pLM SAEs. We ask a minimal, defensible question: can interpretable features causally control epistasis, or only additive traits? Our one primary hypothesis, with a single fallback, is that additive control succeeds while coupling control is at best weakly steerable—an 'epistasis blind spot': steering to install a target coupling (a compensatory pair, a contact-based or long-range functional linkage) reliably shifts additive properties while the intended coupling fails to form, invisible to single-mutant checks but exposed by a double-mutant-cycle oracle. Epistasis is uniquely suited because it is exactly quantifiable (epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning data. Using ESM-2 with TopK and Ordered sparse autoencoders, we LOCATE additive and coupling features, CAUSALLY contrast their steerability, quantify the blind spot, and AUDIT whether an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs. The concrete workflow change if the blind spot holds: engineers steering pLMs should audit couplings with double-mutant-cycle-style checks before synthesis. Either result is publishable—a steerable coupling handle would directly enable compensatory/allosteric design; a clean negative, replicated across models and oracles, delimits what feature-steering can control.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. ADDITIVE oracles: single-mutant effect on GRAVY, net charge, and a stability proxy (fine-tuned ddG head or FoldX), plus ESM-2 single-mutant log-likelihood. EPISTASIS oracle (exact operational definition): the double-mutant-cycle term epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B, taken from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning (DMS) landscapes with measured double mutants - GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535,000 double mutants) plus 2-3 further combinatorial-DMS landscapes from ProteinGym-style resources - and from FoldX for position pairs not experimentally covered; the pLM categorical-Jacobian gives an internal pairwise-coupling read. In-silico epsilon is validated against measured doubles on the DMS-covered subset and strong claims restricted to where they agree. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful RANGE of couplings. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - single-position (additive) features are causally steerable): Identify additive features (correlate with a single position's property, controlling for context; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer to raise a target additive property (e.g., GRAVY) at a chosen position. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target additive effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, within the validity budget). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over control for >=2/3 of features => additive control genuine (H1 holds); [0.2,0.4) over control => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - epistasis is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering to install a coupling silently changes additive properties while the coupling fails to form): (a) DECODABILITY: probe the pairwise epistasis magnitude / categorical-Jacobian coupling of a position pair, controlling for the two positions' additive effects via partial correlation; AUROC. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best coupling direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means high-vs-low-coupling, activation-patching from strongly-coupled sequences, additive-orthogonalized direction) to install a target epistasis at a position pair while holding the two positions' additive contributions fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-DECOUPLING RATE = fraction of coupling-steered, valid sequences whose double-mutant-cycle epsilon did not form (|Delta epsilon| below oracle noise) or formed wrong-sign while additive properties shifted; and ratio r = coupling efficacy / additive efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: coupling decodable (AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 AND decoupling >= 0.30 => epistasis blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a steerable epistasis handle exists, refuting H2 (equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - single-mutant checks miss the failure but the exact double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, compare what a practitioner would inspect against ground truth. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between the additive-property change / single-mutant scores / pseudo-perplexity and the true change in double-mutant-cycle epsilon. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => single-mutant checks are blind to the coupling failure while the double-mutant-cycle oracle reveals it (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; |rho| >= 0.40 => single-mutant checks already flag it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, contact-based (short-range) vs long-range functional couplings; test whether steerability is worse long-range than for contacts; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.

PRE-REGISTERED DEFINITIONS. 'Steerability' of a coupling = on-target |Delta epsilon| exceeding oracle noise AND correct sign at the alpha maximizing on-target change within the validity budget; 'blind spot' = single-mutant/pseudo-perplexity checks show |rho| <= 0.20 with true Delta epsilon while the double-mutant-cycle oracle shows the coupling failed. DMS SELECTION & COUNTS: primary landscape GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535k doubles); add 2-3 combinatorial-DMS landscapes with measured doubles from ProteinGym-style resources; test >=200 position pairs per landscape spanning weak/strong |epsilon|; estimate oracle noise from DMS replicate variance. We SEPARATE claims measured on real DMS doubles from FoldX-derived claims (FoldX used only where doubles are experimentally uncovered, reported separately).

ADDED CONTROLS: random SAE directions, matched-activation-norm directions, single-mutant-only targets (should show no coupling), and a black-box raw-activation probe/edit baseline. ABLATION (indirection test): verify apparent coupling steering is not merely indirect movement on additive traits or sequence likelihood—regress Delta epsilon on the induced additive shifts and on Delta log-likelihood; genuine coupling control must survive this partialling-out. CAUSAL vs PREDICTIVE internal signal: the audit signal is validated by INTERVENTION (does raising the coupling-probe read actually raise measured epsilon?), not correlation alone.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Epistasis has an exact operational definition (double-mutant cycle), but its measurement relies on either DMS data (limited combinatorial double-mutant coverage) or in-silico stability predictors (FoldX/Rosetta), which are proxies; we validate in-silico epistasis against measured double mutants on the DMS-covered subset and restrict strong claims to where they agree, framing claims as model-internal, oracle-verified coupling controllability rather than wet-lab function. 2) The coupling-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, additive-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span an epistasis range, and head-to-head calibrating that ADDITIVE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null coupling result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable epistasis handle) is equally publishable and directly enables compensatory/allosteric design. 3) Additive and epistatic effects are partly entangled; the partial-correlation feature selection and additive-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely additive-independent coupling signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Double-mutant-cycle evaluation is combinatorially heavier than single-mutant checks; we cap position pairs and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (categorical Jacobian), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal coupling probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (additive-steerable, epistasis-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If coupling steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLM epistasis is a controllable design lever.

Name: magnitude_dial_blindspot
Title: On/Off but Not How-Much: Do Interpretable Features Give a Calibrated Magnitude Dial for Scientific Design, or Only a Presence Switch?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific sequence/graph generative models represent a design property's categorical PRESENCE as a cleanly causally-steerable feature, but we hypothesize they do NOT hold a calibrated internal representation of its quantitative MAGNITUDE. One crisp, falsifiable claim: for the SAME property and the SAME steering direction, steering moves the property monotonically yet cannot dial it to a specified numeric target (a set-point calibration failure), and the internal magnitude code is logarithmically compressed so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes. We name this the 'magnitude blind spot' and define it operationally before experiments: presence-flip success is high while numeric set-point hit-rate is low, with set-point error rising with the requested value. Consequently 'set logP to 2.5' or 'set helix content to 40%' silently misses while presence/validity checks pass. Separate contributions: the FINDING (presence-steerable, magnitude-uncalibrated), an INTERPRETATION (log-compression), a FIX (log-reparameterized dial, evaluated on held-out targets), and an AUDIT (internal magnitude-consistency flag).
Related Work: A robust cognitive-science-inspired line shows LLMs encode numeric magnitude in low-dimensional, logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspaces (Language Models Represent Space and Time 2023; The Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024, which causally intervenes on numeric-comparison subspaces; Number Representations in LLMs 2025 showing sublinear/log compression; Numeric Magnitude Comparison Effects 2023 showing human-like distance/size effects). Separately, interpretability-of-generation for scientific objects (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025) steers features toward a property and evaluates whether the property is INCREASED or PRESENT, always reporting directional/binary gains and never a QUANTITATIVE set-point. No prior work (a) transfers the log-compressed magnitude-representation phenomenon from text LLMs into scientific GENERATIVE design, (b) distinguishes presence-steerability from calibrated magnitude-steerability for the same property, or (c) exposes that hitting a numeric design set-point is an unrecognized blind spot with a level-dependent (worse-at-high-magnitude) failure profile. This is distinct from my prior proposals, which contrast intrinsic vs relational/global/pathway properties; here the contrast is categorical presence vs quantitative magnitude of the SAME property, and it borrows a specific human-numeracy finding. Compact contrast: [directional/binary property steering] InterPLM/ProtSAE/chemistry-LM SAEs/Steering-PLMs—report the property increased or is PRESENT; [numeric magnitude in text LLMs] Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024 / Number Representations 2025—log-compressed, causally-manipulable magnitude subspaces, but in TEXT, not generative scientific design; [THIS proposal] exact numeric SET-POINT steering of the SAME property, exposing a level-dependent calibration failure. The delta from steering work is not a new property or direction but target-VALUE calibration and high-end degradation. Who uses it: interpretability researchers, protein/chemistry generative-model builders, and benchmark authors (set-point error as a new axis).
